target.title: fix(cli): reject --channel/--to for systemEvent cron jobs with a clear error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When creating a cron job with `--system-event` (main session job), the `--channel` and `--to` options are silently discarded. Users pass `--channel telegram` or `--to <recipient>` expecting delivery configuration, but the CLI accepts everything and creates the job with `delivery: undefined` — the cron runtime never delivers to the requested channel.

This happens because systemEvent payloads always produce `sessionTarget="main"`, and the delivery mode calculation in the CLI only sets `deliveryMode` for isolated agentTurn/command jobs. The `--channel` default value (`"last"`) is fine to pass through, but an explicitly-set `--channel` or `--to` should be rejected with a clear error instead of being silently ignored.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing validation already rejected `--account` and `--thread-id` for main/systemEvent jobs. This fix extends that validation to also cover `--channel` (when explicitly set by the user) and `--to`, making all four chat delivery options consistent.

## User Impact

- **Before**: `openclaw cron add --name test --every 1h --system-event wakeup --channel telegram` → CLI validation passes silently, job is created with no delivery
- **After**: same command → clear error: `--channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.`
- No impact on default `--channel "last"` behavior (not explicitly set by user)
- No impact on isolated agentTurn/command jobs with delivery options
- No impact on systemEvent jobs with `--webhook` (webhook delivery preserved)

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof: before/after CLI transcript

**Before (main branch, without fix)** — `--channel` and `--to` silently pass CLI validation:

```
$ openclaw cron add --name "before-channel" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --channel telegram
# CLI validation passed (no rejection error)
# GatewayTransportError: gateway closed ... (Gateway not running, unrelated)
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "before-to" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --to "+1234567890"
# CLI validation passed (no rejection error)  
EXIT: 1
```

**After (fix branch)** — `--channel` and `--to` are rejected with clear error:

```
$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-channel" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --channel telegram
Error: --channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-to" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --to "+1234567890"
Error: --channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-webhook" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --webhook "https://example.com/hook"
# CLI validation passed (webhook delivery preserved for systemEvent jobs)
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-nochannel" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup"
# CLI validation passed (default channel="last" is not explicitly set)
EXIT: 1
```

### Regression tests (9 new tests in `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.test.ts`)

All 9 tests pass, covering:
- `--channel` explicitly set → rejected for systemEvent jobs
- `--to` explicitly set → rejected for systemEvent jobs
- `--account` → rejected for systemEvent jobs (existing behavior verified)
- `--thread-id` → rejected for systemEvent jobs (existing behavior verified)
- SystemEvent job without `--channel` → allowed (default value preserved)
- SystemEvent job with `--webhook` → allowed (webhook delivery preserved)
- `--channel` + `--webhook` combined → first guard wins, rejected
- `--channel` for isolated agentTurn → allowed
- `--to` for isolated agentTurn → allowed

### Root cause traced

- `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts:339-352` — the guard only checked `accountId || hasThreadId`, but `hasChatDeliveryTarget` already included `optionSource("channel") === "cli"` and `typeof opts.to === "string"`. The fix extends the guard to include all four conditions.
- `src/cron/delivery-plan.ts:106-123` — `resolveCronDeliveryPlan` returns `{mode:"none"}` for any job that is not isolated+agentTurn/command
- `src/cron/service/jobs.ts:389-401` — `assertDeliverySupport` explicitly rejects channel delivery config for non-isolated session targets

### Test results

- All 9 new regression tests pass
- All existing cron-cli tests pass (85 tests across 8 test files)
- Lint and format checks pass
